changes.procedural_support: Moderate recoverable loads generate a short step from capture-point deficit and incident direction. One shoe lifts while the opposite support is held by two-bone IK. Bounded speed, reach, lateral separation, committed smooth release and cooldown avoid jumps and crossed legs. The lower shoe stays loaded when its partner is already swinging; hand constraints and close bodies block a conflicting free step. Planning integrates once per tick; repeated native candidate evaluation is idempotent. Fast sprint uses native protective reactions; falls clear generated anchors before get-up. Native support travel/lift commits a smooth release instead of dragging an old anchor; restart/root relocations clear anchors and disturbance momentum.
changes.walking: The approved progressive walking range now also carries lower arms, straighter elbows, trunk counterrotation and reduced vertical bob. The existing overlapping-support leg cycle, real shoe marker, cadence and full-stick/RB speeds remain. CPU slow approaches can select the same native-rig walk.
changes.receiving: Designated CPU receivers orient, adjust their arrival step and brake at a forecast meeting point instead of only looking toward the ball. Native trap candidates and skin gates still decide contact. Anticipatory procedural control and real native receipt events recruit torso/arms; accidental response uses lower restitution and bounds muscular surface velocity relative to root travel.
changes.grip: Either real hand may establish contact. The contacting hand then takes over target tracking from its current final anatomical pose, without moving it instantly; only that same arm can maintain the hold. This common acquisition/continuation logic applies to human and CPU. Original skin-distance, joint limits, reciprocal traction and escape remain.
changes.keeper: Small anticipatory hand reaches aim 30 mm into the expected ball path, instead of fragile 15 mm tangency, through the same bounded visible shoulder solver and real-skin contact gate; acceptance tolerance is unchanged.
changes.headers: Native head-contact clips receive load/follow-through offsets that are zero at the exact authored impact. Header-specific speed depends on input/charge, incoming ball and actual head-surface motion, capped at 13 m/s for passes and 18 m/s for shots. The human foot-pass speed override excludes headers. CPU contenders and wide crossing options have broader eligibility while respecting nearer teammates.
changes.learned_muscles: Keep the approved six-unit, 18-weight trained angular servo. A wider 75-generation candidate slightly reduced weighted cost but worsened RMS and acceleration variation against that servo, so its runtime weights were rejected. Procedural foot planning is analytical IK combined with learned upper-body muscles, not a learned whole-body policy.

learned_motor.algorithm: cross-entropy neural policy search on perturbed angular dynamics
learned_motor.scope: Learned upper-body angular servo with native motion references and domain-randomized reduced dynamics. Not Euphoria, AMP, a trained whole-body locomotion/balance policy, or proof of full-body sim-to-game transfer.

rejected_policy_experiment.reason: Held-out angular RMS and acceleration variation regressed against the previous learned motor; keep approved runtime weights.

superseded_test_outcomes.reason: The extra receipt assertion counted traps only and omitted valid first-time passes. Join an actual native contact to the previous pass target so one-touch receptions count too; retain the requirement for at least two distinct CPU actors and quantified torso/arm response. Same binary, no reduced contact or movement thresholds.

preflight_findings.finding: Restricting acquisition to an already-selected reach arm prevented a valid CPU contact by its other hand. Unify acquisition and continuation: adopt the actual contacting hand with no pose displacement, track it through the hold and measure continuation on that arm. Both human grip and CPU grip suites retain their original real-distance/force/escape conditions.

The two-second observation reset at t=43100 after a long cross selected at t=42840 with contact frame 46, before its expected t=43300 impact. Every trial now uses the same fixed three-second post-release observation, retaining exactly-one-kick and unchanged real-skin tolerances.

One central save missed the actual skin by 0.00552 m. The visible bounded shoulder reach now targets slightly deeper into the trajectory, without enlarging contact tolerance. Moving/repositioned source roots also release/reset obsolete support anchors. All keeper fixtures are rerun in the final binary.

An upright-mode fixture requested a falling-only renderer event; its four support directions and anatomy passed. The fixture now explicitly interrupts a generated step with a fall/get-up and checks that renderer.

Free recovery could compete with a close hand/body constraint. After gating free steps, a second issue remained: the idle hand could transiently satisfy the grip distance while a different arm was tracking the shirt. Restrict attachment to the active hand; keep original distance, force, slowdown, escape and anatomy assertions. Both issues are rerun in the final binary.

investigated_findings: A retimed leg cycle alone retained jogging arms and root bounce. Upper-body walking is now derived on the same native rig and the three stick-strength rendered tests verify continuous motion and ball connection.

Head passes inherited foot-specific power and lacked preparation because an additive contact guard correctly froze the head chain. Baking a load which crosses zero at the native impact preserves that marker while showing preparation and follow-through. Both directed-header suites verify actual contact, aim and the bounded head-specific power.

Skin transitions could supply an artificial 18 m/s muscular surface velocity and strong rebounds. The new bound applies to local surface motion relative to travel; native intentional receipt records and CPU arrival adjustment address control rather than only passive collision.

Procedural supports must be cleared on a fall; otherwise a recovered actor can resume an old world-space step. Numeric interruption/get-up coverage and the final rendered support fixture verify anchor clearing.

The learned candidate was not shipped as an improvement on the strength of weighted cost alone. Its worse held-out angular RMS and acceleration variation caused rejection; runtime policy/trainer/weights remain byte-identical to the approved release.

All 33 release scenarios use the exact native hash recorded above. Earlier preflights and interrupted queues are excluded. One same-hash runner stopped before producing a result and was restarted; no incomplete suite is counted. The corrected fixture outcomes below retain their prior failure explanations.
limits: Windows is cross-compiled and statically package-validated. Rendered tests run on Linux/X11 with a virtual Xbox controller and null OpenAL audio; Windows rendering and physical-controller feel still need the user PC.

The trained servo is a reduced angular model, not whole-body reinforcement learning, muscular biomechanics, Euphoria or proof of human motion equivalence. The new recovery-step planner is analytical, with explicit game-calibrated limits.
Generated procedural profiles and catalogued metadata pairs are not new motion captures or exhaustive visual validation. Native animation still owns normal locomotion and football action selection.

Foot support is bounded and can release for actions, fast running, held bodies or loss of balance. The system does not guarantee recovery from any impulse or perfect sole adhesion through all animation blends.

The approved controlled-ground-dribble collision exemption remains. Real skin gates and anatomy checks do not establish universal absence of interpenetration, every reception or every possible match situation.
